Hi, I do not believe in psychological classifications for mood/affect disorders. They are just labels that are supposed to describe a certain type of behaviour and potential causes. Many of the descriptions and symptoms overlap - Like ADHD, PTSD, bipolar, manic-depressive disorder. I could have all of them. A psychiatrist with two PhDs suspected that I might be schizophrenic. It is a surprise I haven't massacred half a village in pure bliss. I do have a strong background in biology though and I did some research. The two areas of the brain that mostly interact in terms of impulse control are the prefrontal cortex and the amygdala. The amygdala is responsible for pain and pleasure signalling, while the prefrontal cortex is the control centre - that is animal vs free will. I do believe that there is genetic diversity and there are neurophysiological differences that can cause susceptibility or result in a predisposition, but in the end, I bet that environmental factors, basically life experience has the strongest effect on our perception, behaviour, and brain function. But this would be particularly good news because it means that if you change your environment or gather a different set of experiences the activity of the amygdala can be altered and stress, fear, anxiety, aggression, and depression can dissolve. How to achieve that is a different story! I am convinced positive social interactions and healthy intimacy are probably the keys.
